tagline: East Africa's flagship island, by foil.
summary: Zanzibar is East Africa's premier island destination — Stone Town's UNESCO waterfront, the northern beach resorts, and the marine-protected diving around Mnemba — reliant on one of the region's busiest mainland crossings. It fits the Indian Ocean luxury archetype alongside Seychelles and Mauritius.

use_cases.title: Resort transfers
use_cases.body: Direct foiling resort runs up the coast — Nungwi (~30 nm), Mnemba (~28 nm) — beating long roads.

use_cases.title: Mainland crossing
use_cases.body: A faster, smoother, all-weather Dar es Salaam↔Stone Town (~38 nm) crossing.

use_cases.title: Island-hopping
use_cases.body: Inter-island links to Pemba (~45 nm) and the dive sites.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Intra-island and resort transfers (Nungwi ~30 nm, Mnemba ~28 nm, Pemba ~45 nm) sit inside the all-electric envelope over warm protected water; low-wake foiling protects the reef-fringed coast.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries the busy mainland crossing (Dar↔Stone Town ~38 nm) all-weather with no charging at either terminal.

competitive_landscape: Today: diesel fast-ferries on the Dar crossing and conventional speedboats for resort transfers and island-hopping. The pain is rough, smoky, weather-limited boats around a fragile reef — the status quo a clean, smooth tier improves on.
seasonality: NE monsoon (Dec–Mar) and SE monsoon (Jun–Sep) shape sea state; the hybrid handles the mainland crossing year-round, intra-island runs flex with conditions.
regulatory_note: Tanzania's tourism and marine authorities license the Dar–Zanzibar route and resort transfers; the Mnemba marine-protected area favours low-impact zero-emission vessels — aligning with conservation mandates.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network, not just a pilot.
